hints.content:
###Graphing the first point

To graph a line, we need to find two points that are on it. Then we can drag the movable points to those points.

We already have one point, $(6,7)$, and we can use the slope of the line to find another point.

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The point six, seven is plotted and labeled.

hints.content:
###Use the slope to graph another point

We want the slope to be $2$:

$\text{slope}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\text{rise}}}{\maroonD{\text{run}}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\Delta y}}{\maroonD{\Delta x}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{2}}{\maroonD{1}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{-2}}{\maroonD{-1}}$

Starting at $(6,7)$, we don't have room on the given grid to go $2$ units up and $1$ unit right. So let's go $\purpleD{2\text{ units down}}$ and $\maroonD{1\text{ unit to the left}}$ to plot another point on the line:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The points six, seven and five, five are plotted and labeled. There is a vertical dotted segment from six, seven to six, five that is labeled negative two. There is a horizontal dotted segment from six, five to five, five that is labeled negative one.

question.content:
**Graph a line that contains the point $(6,7)$ and has a slope of $2$.**
